text: Flamingos do not bend their knees backward. What appears to be a knee is actually their ankle joint.
A single day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than a Venusian year (225 Earth days).
Humans glow faintly in the dark, but the light emitted is 1,000x weaker than what our eyes can detect.
Cleopatra lived closer to the invention of the iPhone than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
Octopuses can adjust to cold by editing their RNA.
Saturn has 274 confirmed moons, with Titan being the largest.
The intestine regenerates its lining, called the epithelium, every 5 to 7 days.
The first computer bug was a literal moth trapped in a Harvard Mark II computer in 1947.
Plants can retain information from past experiences and use this 'memory' to respond to environmental changes.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at 3.8 cm (1.5 inches) per year.
Your aorta, the body's largest artery, is roughly as wide as a garden hose.
Ancient Romans used fermented human urine as a cleaning agent to remove grease stains from clothing.
Dolphins develop a unique signature whistle early in life to identify each other.
Neutron stars are so incredibly dense that a single teaspoon of their matter would weigh approximately 6 billion tons.
The human brain is about 75% water, which is why staying hydrated is essential for optimal cognitive function.
The first webcam was invented to monitor a coffee pot at Cambridge University.
An elephant's trunk is a complex network of 40,000 muscles, compared to just 600 in the entire human body.
Pluto features a distinctive heart-shaped glacier named Sputnik Planitia.
Your salivary glands produce between 1 and 1.5 liters of saliva every day.
In the 17th-century, condoms were commonly made from animal intestines, particularly from sheep, calves, or goats.
Polar bears have black skin underneath their white fur, which helps them absorb and retain heat from sunlight.
The Sun's core temperature reaches around 15 million °C (27 million °F), hot enough to sustain nuclear fusion.
Nearly 60% of the human brain consists of fat, making essential fatty acids vital for brain health.
The word 'robot' originates from the Czech word 'robota', which means 'forced labor'.
The immortal jellyfish can reverse its aging process and revert to its juvenile stage.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a massive storm that has been continuously raging for at least 150 years.
The cornea is the only part of the human body with no blood supply—it receives oxygen directly from the air.
The first photograph was taken in 1826 and required at least 8 hours of exposure.
Blue whales have the largest heart of any animal on Earth, weighing about 181 kg (400 pounds).
Mars has the tallest volcano in our solar system — Olympus Mons — rising about 22 km (14 mi) high.
Your tongue print is as unique as your fingerprint, with no two people having identical patterns.
The microwave was invented by accident after an engineer noticed a magnetron tube melted a candy bar in his pocket.
Butterflies taste with their feet, using special sensors to identify whether plants are suitable for laying eggs.
The coldest known place in the universe is the Boomerang Nebula, which has a temperature of about −272°C (-458°F).
Your taste buds regenerate every 10 to 14 days.
A tree absorbs anywhere between 10 and 40kg of CO2 per year.
Crows can remember human faces and hold grudges for up to 17 years.
On the Moon, you would weigh approximately 16.5% of your weight on Earth due to its lower gravity.
Atoms never truly stop moving, even at absolute zero—they just reach their lowest quantum vibrations.
The tiny bumps on the F and J keyboard keys help touch-typists locate the home position.
A shrimp's heart is located in its head rather than its body.
The Milky Way galaxy is about 100,000 light-years in diameter.
Helium is the only element that stays liquid at absolute zero unless high pressure is applied.
Phytoplankton produce about half of Earth's oxygen and help absorb carbon dioxide in the air.
Three-toed sloths can hold their breath underwater for up to 40 minutes by slowing their heart rate.
Venus rotates clockwise, which is the opposite direction from most planets in our solar system.
Fire tornadoes can reach core temperatures of up to 1,090°C (2,000°F).
Golf balls have dimples to reduce air resistance and allow the ball to fly farther.
Koalas have fingerprints that are remarkably similar to human fingerprints.
Germany's V-2 rocket became the first human-made object to reach space in 1944.
Petrichor is the earthy smell produced when rain falls on dry soil.
The small pocket inside jeans was originally designed to hold pocket watches in the 1800s.
Dark oxygen is oxygen produced in the deep ocean without sunlight.
The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth at 27,300 km/h (17,000 mph).
Lava is not nearly hot enough to melt a diamond.
Male seahorses carry and give birth to their young, not the females.
Moonquakes are seismic tremors that occur on the Moon, similar to earthquakes but generally much weaker.
Pure gallium metal has such a low melting point that it will melt in your hand.
The number 142,857 is cyclic—when multiplied by 1 through 6, it produces the same six digits in a rotating sequence.
Despite their extremely long necks, giraffes have the same number of vertebrae as humans.
Earwax can contain valuable indicators to a person's health, such as potential risks for certain diseases.
Planck time is the shortest measurable time interval—approximately 5.39 × 10⁻⁴⁴ seconds.
The Marree Man, a 3.5km geoglyph of a hunter, appeared mysteriously in the Australian desert in 1998.
Light takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to travel from the Sun to Earth.
Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring material on Earth.
Wood frogs can freeze solid in winter and thaw back to life in spring.
The Kármán line marks the boundary between Earth's atmosphere and space at 100 km (62 mi) altitude.
Hydrogen makes up roughly 75% of the observable universe.
The snailfish is the deepest recorded fish species, which was filmed at a depth of 8,336 meters (27,349 feet).
The ISS orbits Earth once every 92 min, which allows astronauts to see as many as 16 sunrises and sunsets a day.
The word 'laser' stands for 'Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation'.
The first photo of Earth from space was taken in 1946 by a V-2 rocket.
The smallest possible black hole could be as small as an atom but have the mass of a large mountain.
It takes about 12 worker bees their entire lives to produce a single teaspoon of honey.

The mimic octopus can impersonate more than 15 different marine species to avoid predators.

The oldest known DNA ever found on earth dates back approximately 2 million years.
Monotremes are the only group of living mammals that reproduce by laying eggs.

Any month that starts on a Sunday contains a Friday the 13th.
The word 'astronaut' comes from the Greek astron ('star') and nautēs ('sailor'), literally meaning 'star sailor'.
Prolonged focus on a repetitive task can shape our thoughts and dreams—a phenomenon called the Tetris Effect.
Hyperion, the tallest tree on Earth, towers over the Statue of Liberty by about 22 meters.
The fastest known neutron star spins 716 times per second—faster than most kitchen blenders.
The bee hummingbird is the smallest living bird and produces eggs as small as coffee beans.

The whale shark is the largest fish in the world, capable of growing up to 18 meters (60 feet).
People tend to assume their own opinions and habits are more common than they actually are—a bias called the false-consensus effect.
Ants can carry 10 to 50 times their body weight due to their high ratio of muscle tissue to body mass.
Antarctica is the only continent without reptiles or snakes.
The hummingbird is the only bird capable of sustained backward flight.
Lake Vostok is Antarctica's largest known subglacial lake, buried beneath about 4 km (2.5 mi) of ice.
There's an orchestra made up entirely of typewriters.
Some tourists who visit Paris develop extreme symptoms when the city does not live up to their expectations.
Airlines typically require pilots to eat different meals to avoid both getting sick from potential food poisoning.
You can make diamonds out of peanut butter by mimicking the extreme conditions found deep within Earth.
The human chin remains an evolutionary mystery.
CAPTCHA stands for 'Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart'.
Each person's scent is unique, influenced by factors such as genetics, diet, and health.
